entry.name: Orange and Apples
entry.description: Heisenberg's own 1927 analogy, built so a visitor has to perform it. A low bench holds a tray of eighteen identical dark knobs under a cantilevered hood; three of them are apples and the rest are decoys, made from the SAME mesh with the SAME material instance, so which is which cannot be read off the surface. Beside the bench stands a rack of oranges, and an orange is a grabbable throwable in both lanes - RMB and LMB on the desktop crosshair, grip and trigger in the headset. A struck apple registers WHERE it was, as a lit pin standing on the tray floor, and in the same instant takes a kick in a direction nobody chose. Position is bought with momentum. THE TRADE IS THE OBJECT AND NOT A CAPTION ON IT: on the panel above, a single outlined rectangle has WIDTH = the spread on position and HEIGHT = the spread on momentum, and its AREA NEVER CHANGES - squeeze it narrow and it has to grow tall. Above that rectangle sits the same rectangle drawn four times at four widths, dim, as a printed scale, so a still photograph shows the law without anyone touching anything. Impact speed sets all of it from one number, which is the actual content of the 1927 argument rather than decoration on it: a fast orange is a short wavelength, so it resolves the apple to a hairline pin and a narrow rectangle AND shoves it harder; a gentle one barely tells you anything and barely moves it. There is no throw that buys the first without paying the second. The concealment is geometry, never shadow - an unlit box photographs as a black rectangle and hall lighting is not a constant across this museum - so the apples hide in a CROWD, under a roof that cuts the sight line to the back rows. Note the sizes: the orange is 10.4 cm and the apple is 9.0 cm, and the probe being bigger than the thing probed is the reason the disturbance cannot be made small.
dev_themes: a look is done WITH something, and the something arrives
the record of a measurement outlives the state it recorded
a rectangle of constant area is the whole relation, and it survives a still
entry.qfep_connection: The laboratory's other observer-effect piece, two_point_ruler, makes the OPPOSITE claim and the pair are worth standing near each other: there the subject is honest throughout - it never changes, so nothing about the reading is wrong - and the displacement lands on a bystander you can only catch by looking away from your own instrument. Here the displacement lands on the thing measured, which is Heisenberg's case rather than Schroedinger's, and there is no innocent subject anywhere in the room. Together they say the two things QFEP wants said about measurement at once: that an instrument alters what it is not pointed at, and that it alters what it is.
interactions: Look into the hood before throwing anything. Eighteen identical knobs, and the question the artifact asks is already fully posed: which three of these are apples? Nothing about the surface answers it.
Throw gently. The pin comes up fat, the rectangle stays broad and flat, and the apple barely shifts. You have learned roughly where something was and cost it almost nothing.
Throw hard. The pin is a hairline, the rectangle stands up narrow and tall, and the apple leaves fast in a direction you did not choose. Same gauge, opposite proportions, same area.

Come back to the pins after four or five throws. There is one per apple, standing where that apple was when you last measured it and describing nothing presently in the tray - each was made by the act that emptied its own spot. It is not a growing bed: a second reading on the same apple moves its pin, because a record that accumulated would fill the tray and you could no longer see into it.
Place it once with #mode:open. The roof is gone, the apples are visible, no throw is needed and the instrument has nothing to say. That is the control condition and it is worth walking.

config.mode: hood | open | deep - how hidden the apples are. `open` removes the roof and cheeks entirely and is the artifact's own control condition. `deep` reaches 16 cm further forward and drops 6 cm, hiding more WITHOUT narrowing the aperture; lowering the roof instead was tried first and left a 9 cm slot, which a 10.4 cm orange cannot enter.
config.cols: 2-9, default 6 - columns in the bed of knobs.
config.rows: 1-4, default 3 - rows in the bed. cols x rows is the size of the crowd the three apples hide in, which is what 'hard to find' actually means here.
config.count: 1-8, default 4 - oranges on the rack. The rack is SIZED from this, so a bigger magazine is a longer shelf and never two oranges spawned inside each other.

entry.config_note: Every key is either word-valued (mode) or already in GridInteractablesComponent.CONFIG_PARAM_NAMES (rows, cols, count), so none can be eaten by the tutorial's #key:number shorthand. The number of APPLES is deliberately not a config key: it is three because the source says three, and a numeric #apples:3 is not in that list, so it would be read as tutorial_id:rotation, leave the artifact at its default and make the map token look correct while doing nothing.

spatial_needs.clearance_note: The front clearance is 3 and it is not padding. A visitor has to stand back far enough to throw an orange on an arc into a 28 cm slot; at 1 cell they are leaning over the tray and can only drop. This is the one artifact in the room whose clearance is a fact about a trajectory rather than about a sightline.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry at the shipped defaults, no Godot was run for this figure. Width: the assembly is centred on the origin by construction (_bench_x derives the offset rather than typing it), running from bench_x - SLAB.x/2 to rack_x + shelf/2, and at count 4 the shelf is 4 x 0.128 + 0.06 = 0.572, so bench_x = -0.336 and the span is -1.036 to 1.036. Height: SLAB_TOP 0.78 + PANEL.y 1.12 = 1.90, and the readout plate tops out at 1.82 inside it. Depth: the back panel's rear face at -0.29 to the caption screen's glass at +0.245, with the hood roof reaching +0.24 and the tray's front rim +0.255. `deep` mode pushes the roof to +0.40 and takes the depth to 0.69; `open` removes it and leaves 0.545 unchanged. A larger #count lengthens the shelf and widens the whole box by the same amount at BOTH ends, because the centring is derived - at count 8 the width is 2.584 and the origin is still the middle.

entry.note: Built 2026-09-09. Physics contract, because it is the part a later editor will break by tidying: apples are RigidBody3D on collision_layer 1 with mask 1|4 - layer 1 so the orange's shipped pickable mask (196615) reaches them, and deliberately NOT layer 3, since an apple on the grab layer could be lifted out and read with the hand, which is the one thing this bench must not allow. Decoys are StaticBody3D on layer 1. Oranges are instances of addons/godot-xr-tools/objects/pickable.tscn with their collision layer and mask left exactly as shipped (layer 3, which is what DesktopInteractionPointer.GRAB_MASK 393220 and the VR hand both look for); a bare RigidBody3D was the cheaper build and was rejected because function_pickup.gd:294 rejects anything without a pick_up() method before it reaches the grab list, so a plain body can be carried on desktop and never lifted in the headset. Contact monitoring lives on the ORANGE, not on the eighteen knobs, and the impact speed used for the reading is the one recorded at the top of the physics frame - by the time body_entered is emitted the step has already resolved the bounce and linear_velocity is what the fruit is doing on its way back out. The throw is action_pressed to charge and action_released to release, connected at build time because DesktopInteractionPointer._fires refuses to call action() at all unless the signal already has a listener; a charge held past CHARGE_S + 0.45 s launches anyway, so a lost release event cannot strand the fruit in a visitor's hand. NO dna.axes block: this artifact has never been swept and the declaration gate has never been run against it, and a hand-typed axis that does not match the code is the fault this project most often catches in itself.

entry.name: Random Cubes
entry.description: Chaotically arranged cubes representing high entropy. Random positions, rotations, scales.

dna.default: macrostate=uniform, chance=all - uniform is the `_:` branch of _region_plan() and returns the one shipped region lo=(-r, 0, -r) hi=(r, r, r), so the three randf_range calls draw from the same ranges in the same order; chance=all draws size, hue and spin exactly as before; and the wire bounds frame is built ONLY when macrostate != uniform, so the default adds no node. All three placements (QFEP_E_Term, Corridor_QFEP_E_Term, Curation_Bay_qfeplaboratory_4) are bare tokens, and apply_grid_config returns before rebuilding unless a key is present AND its value differs AND _ready has already built. THE PILE WAS NEVER THE SAME TWICE: the artifact is unseeded by design, so `exact' here means the same code path and the same distribution, which is the strongest sense available. chance_seed defaults to 0, which keeps the global RNG - only the sweep's fixture pins it.
dna.was: six exports and no apply_grid_config, so nothing was reachable from a map token. Every export was a dimension, a rate or a colour: cube_count, spawn_radius, size_min, size_max, drift_speed, base_color. The two decisions that carry the argument - WHICH region the cubes occupy and WHAT is left to the dice - were written inline in the spawn loop.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-04, refused by the runner as NO TURNABLE KNOBS. BOTH WORDS ARE BORROWED, neither invented. macrostate = uniform|corner|layered|spilled is microstate_counter's axis, character for character - the artifact in this same sequence whose entire job is to print log10(W) for exactly these four arrangements. Entropy is not a property of a pile, it is a count of the ways the pile could have been, and that count does not exist until you say which macrostate you are counting: the same twenty cubes crowded into one octant are just as randomly placed and have vastly fewer ways to be. chance = none|hue|size|all is john_cage_tech_noir's, and this artifact ships the opposite end of it - that piece surrenders NOTHING visible to chance and defaults to `none`; this one defaults to `all`. One borrowed question, two artifacts standing at its two ends, which is worth more than a private word at each.
dna.orientation_caveat: ORIENTATION RIDES WITH `all`. The borrowed chance list has no value for spin, and forking the list to add one would make the shared word a lie, so none/hue/size all stand their cubes axis-aligned and only `all` tumbles them. Stated because it is the single place the borrowed vocabulary does not cover this artifact exactly. Their angular velocity is zeroed too, not just their initial rotation: a value has to survive being stood in for ten minutes, not only photographed - a random spin would have eroded `aligned' within seconds.
dna.frame_note: THE WIRE BOX IS PART OF THE ARGUMENT AND ONLY THE NON-DEFAULT VALUES GET IT. The spawn volume is invisible in the shipped artifact, so `corner` without a frame is not the same pile confined but simply a smaller pile over there - which is size wearing a name - and `spilled` would have nothing to have spilled out of. microstate_counter draws its amber octant cage for the same stated reason. uniform draws no frame and is therefore untouched.
dna.declined: drift_speed, this file's own declared critical_parameter. At zero the chaos is frozen and above zero it is visibly restless - real, and invisible to a still PNG. info_board was swept across five duration exports and published six identical tiles. Rates stay exports.
dna.fixture_note: WITHOUT chance_seed THE SWEEP MEASURES A DIFFERENT OBJECT PER FRAME. Every position, size, hue and velocity comes from an unseeded global randf, so four values of an axis would be four fresh piles and any difference measured would be the dice, not the axis. chance_seed pins the draw; it defaults to 0, which is the shipped unseeded path, so no placement is affected.
dna.measurement_risk: SPARSE SUBJECT. Twenty cubes of 0.05-0.15 m loose in a 2 x 1 x 2 m volume: the union AABB the sweep frames on is mostly empty air, so a faint verdict here should be crop-rechecked before it is believed (random_walk_collection moved 174 grey levels across 0.06% of frame and read the same as a genuinely inert axis). The wire frame on three of the four macrostate values helps - it puts a fixed, high-contrast reference in the same pixels. `spilled' was deliberately kept close (plume to 1.45r, not 3r) so the union does not shrink the other three values to specks.

entry.qfep_connection: Cubes in chaotic disarray — high entropy as furniture, random positions and rotations and scales. The grid's own elements thrown to the λ=1 wind, order's vocabulary spoken as noise. Between this and the ordered_grid the whole spectrum stretches.

entry.name: Phase Cube
entry.description: A cube that shows phase transitions. SOLID (crystal, λ<0.25) → COMPLEX (edge, 0.25<λ<0.55) → GAS (dissolution, λ>0.55). Visual metaphor for matter states as QFEP states.
entry.qfep_connection: Matter's phase diagram hijacked as pedagogy: two thresholds (λ 0.25 and 0.55) cut a continuum into solid, complex, gas, while a dissolution scalar does the actual becoming between the labels. The cube stays a cube throughout — it is the category that melts.

dna.default: regime=all, occupancy=corridor - all is the one value absent from REGIME_WINDOWS and _apply_regime returns on it immediately, so r_min=2.5 and r_max=4.0 stay exactly as exported, all three regime markers stay inside the corridor and nothing is skipped by the new range guard. corridor is the `_:` branch of _dot_position and is the shipped expression character for character: y = x * (wall_height - 0.5) + 0.25, z scattered across +/- 0.6 * walkway_width. apply_grid_config is guarded three ways (key present, value buildable, value different) and returns before _rebuild_data until _built is true, so the 2 placements - QFEP_Lambda_Spectrum (token bifurcation_walkway:90:0:0.8) and Corridor_QFEP_Lambda_Spectrum - rebuild nothing. ONE DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE, the same one bifurcation_diagram took on 2026-08-03: the z scatter was a bare randf(), so every launch was a different cloud. It is now the identical range from a generator seeded 20260803. Statistically the same corridor, but comparable frame to frame, and without it a sweep of occupancy would be measuring the RNG.
dna.was: No axis exports at all - refused by the runner for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. walkway_length, r_min, r_max, num_columns and dot_size were @export but they are dimensions and resolution, not claims: no map could say anything about WHAT the corridor argues. The r window and the cloud's place in the architecture were both single hard-coded facts.
dna.note: regime crops the r axis onto one behaviour class, and the crop means something different in a corridor than in a chart. A cropped chart is a chart of less; a cropped corridor is twelve metres of one condition. stable = 2.5..3.0 is a corridor you can walk end to end while nothing whatever happens - the transition promised by the title refused, which is the sharpest sentence this artifact has. cascade = 3.0..3.57 puts the whole period-doubling ladder under a twelve-metre walk, so Feigenbaum's constant is legible as the rungs crowding toward the far end. chaos = 3.57..4.0 is the band with the period-3 window standing in it as a stripe of order. period3 = 3.82..3.87 fills the corridor with that window alone, three clean branches inside what the signage calls chaos. occupancy asks where the mathematics meets the body, which is this artifact's whole thesis and the one thing it could not vary: corridor suspends the cloud at head height so you walk THROUGH it and displace it; mural flattens it onto the two side walls and hands you back the chart you were supposed to have escaped, walking past rather than through; inlay drops it into the floor and maps the population value ACROSS the corridor instead of up it, so the cascade branches left and right beneath you and the part you stand on is the part you cannot see; vault lifts it overhead out of reach. Each is a different relation between a body and a parameter, not a different mounting.
dna.kin: regime is bifurcation_diagram's word, taken character for character - the same five values, the same four windows, the same meaning of `all`. That reuse is deliberate and checkable: this artifact and that one are the SAME equation drawn twice, once as a chart on a wall and once as architecture you walk, so if the shared word is honest the two should measure alike under it. Any large divergence in the bite numbers is a finding about the difference between reading a diagram and standing in one. regime is also the wider family word (harmonic_motion_demo, spring_demo, mass_spring_damper, VectorForces, homogeneous_coordinates, DualBallFMController) used for exactly the family's question. The sibling's SECOND axis, trace = attractor|transient|approach, was deliberately NOT taken: skip_transient is right there and it would have transferred mechanically, but it is the chart's question - which drawing of the data is shown - and repeating it here would have produced a second artifact that argues nothing a corridor argues. occupancy is a new word. The nearest existing ones were rejected on meaning: support (none|stand|frame|pylon) and admission (none|bench|residue|exhibit) are furniture words about how a prop is held, and reading this axis as mounting is precisely the error - a walkway's whole claim is embodiment, so where the data sits relative to the walking body IS its argument.
dna.still_note: occupancy should bite hardest - the point cloud is most of the ink and mural, inlay and vault each move all of it into a different half of the frame. regime is strong for the same reason bifurcation_diagram's is: the cloud is redrawn over a different domain and _get_color_for_r re-ramps across it, so the four crops share almost no ink. THE MULTIMESH CAVEAT APPLIES AND IS SEVERE HERE: every dot lives in a MultiMeshInstance3D, which the capture AABB does not count, so the measured extent comes only from the floor slab, the two wall planes, the 24 floor-gradient segments and the three marker bars. Those are the corridor SHELL and they do not move under either axis, so a subject-percentage computed from them will understate the change. The one place that was fatal rather than merely pessimistic is occupancy=vault, where the cloud is lifted to wall_height + 1.55, above every mesh instance in the scene: an unfixed capture would have framed the empty corridor and scored the axis as `the dots were deleted`. _build_frame_anchor adds a layers = 0 box covering the real extent, and ONLY at vault - building it for all four values would inflate the framing of the three that do not need it, which is the same fault reversed.
dna.gotcha: The r readout, the regime name and the floor colour all track a PLAYER who is not present during a headless capture; _process falls back to arrow keys, so a still is always taken at _current_r = r_min with the r and regime labels parked at the corridor entrance. That is time- and input-domain and neither axis touches it - both were chosen to be facts about built geometry, which is there whether or not anyone is walking. Note also that TWO different artifacts are called bifurcation_walkway in this repo: this corridor at commons/interfaces/qfep/, and an unregistered vertical display at commons/artifacts/bifurcation_walkway/ that still carries class_name BifurcationWalkway. Only this one is reachable from a map token; the promotion is on this one.

entry.name: Complexity Pattern
entry.description: Game of Life cellular automata at edge of chaos. Self-organizing complexity.

dna.default: rule=life, readout=relief - life is [[3], [2, 3]], which is B3/S23, which is the `neighbors == 2 or neighbors == 3` that _step_simulation wrote out by hand; relief keeps the shipped 0.5 x cell_size body and the shipped 1.5 lift on a living cell, and is the only readout that leaves mesh.position alone. Neither key is passed by either of the 2 existing placements, and apply_grid_config rebuilds only when a value both validates and differs, so those two rooms are unchanged.
dna.was: no axis at all - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The five exports are grid_size, cell_size, update_interval and two colours: dimensions and decoration. The two decisions that carry the argument were hard-coded one function down, the transition rule in _step_simulation and the elevation in _update_visuals, and there was no apply_grid_config, so a map token could not reach anything.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-03. The @identity names the critical_parameter as initial density (~0.4), and density is the WRONG knob here on both counts: under Life every starting density converges to the same sparse litter of still lifes within twenty generations, so five densities photograph as five indistinguishable fields - the reaction_diffusion failure exactly. The quantity that actually carries lambda is a property of the RULE TABLE, not of the soup. So the axis is the law: life sits at the edge, seeds sprays, replicator fills with periodic fractal texture, maze and coral freeze into standing structure. The artifact stops asserting 'edge of chaos' and starts showing what the two sides of it look like. NOT named `generator` although perlin_noise declares that word for the same slot - a noise basis is sampled once and has no history, these are transition rules whose whole content is what they do to their own output over time.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: perlin_noise, simplex_noise, mandelbrot_set, perlin_noise_terrain, random_edge_profile - readout is relief|plate|column on all of them, same three words, same meaning, and relief is the default on all of them because each shipped code path lifts its sample. This field can therefore be compared with those five rather than merely contrasted.
dna.fixture_note: the field is GENERATIVE and slow. pattern_seed pins the soup, without which six rule variants are six different random starts and the sweep measures the RNG instead of the law. warmup runs 80 generations before the first frame, without which every variant photographs the same undifferentiated 40% soup - no rule has spoken yet at generation 0. Both default to 0 in code, which is the shipped behaviour (fresh randomness, player meets the soup and watches it organise), so they are fixture knobs and not axes.
dna.measurement_risk: the subject is a 0.64 x 0.64 slab about 0.02 thick, so a fit-by-diagonal camera will under-frame it. If the critic reports faint on both axes, check subject % before believing it and add a framing hint rather than re-cutting the axis.

entry.qfep_connection: Conway's Game of Life running at the edge of chaos — self-organizing complexity from the simplest rules. The canonical proof that the edge is real: gliders and oscillators and still lifes, none designed, all emergent, the cellular-automata chapter's crown reappearing here as evidence for the equation's central band.

entry.name: Rigid Sculpture
entry.description: Static crystalline form for φ<0 zone. Resists change.

dna.default: formation=ring - ring is the shipped arrangement line for line: the same (i/element_count)*TAU angle, the same size*0.6 radius, the same outward -angle turn, with the central octahedron and both caps untouched. It is also the _: fallthrough, so an unknown word renders the shipped sculpture rather than blanking it. The one existing placement (QFEP_Phi_Term) passes no keys, and apply_grid_config rebuilds only when a value both validates and differs, and only after _ready has built once, so that room is unchanged.
dna.was: one hard-coded ring of eight prisms around an octahedron, with no apply_grid_config at all - so nothing here was reachable from a map token. The three exports were size, element_count and a colour: dimensions and decoration. The decision that carries the argument, WHICH order this monument keeps, was written inline in the build loop under a comment that said perfect geometric arrangement.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-04, refused by the runner as NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The @identity names the critical_parameter as the ABSENCE OF ANIMATION - and that cannot be an axis, because the evidence is one still PNG: a form that does not move and a form that does are the same photograph. So the axis is the other half of the claim. phi<0 does not merely resist change, it defends a particular order, and the five values are five orders worth defending: a centre held on all sides (ring), repetition without privilege (lattice), closure in every direction (shell), rank (column), and an order that has already weathered and holds its pose anyway (drift). drift is seeded per index, because the shipped code contains no randomness at all and an unseeded draw would make five variants of five objects.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: reactive_particle_field, reactive_particles, edge_particles, emergence_zone (four registry tokens on one scene) and delaunay_triangulation_3d_cell - formation is lattice|shell|ring|column|drift on all of them, same five words, same question: where a set of small elements stands relative to one another. Only the default differs, because this artifact ships the ring and they ship the lattice, so this sculpture can be compared with those five rather than merely contrasted. NOT crystal_cluster's growth (scatter|druse|lattice|vein), which is the nearest artifact in the registry and was hand-promoted for the same reason: growth asks how a mineral GREW and its values are mineralogical events, whereas this is a made monument arguing about imposed order - and its shipped ring is not among growth's four values at all.
dna.measurement_risk: column and shell change the merged AABB (a 0.8 tall stack, a 0.48 sphere) where ring and lattice are flat and wide, so a fit-by-diagonal camera frames them differently. That is honest here - the formation really does change the shape - but do not read the reframing itself as the bite.

entry.qfep_connection: A static crystalline form for the φ<0 zone — not just ordered but *resisting* change, order that has taken a stance against becoming. Where the crystal is merely frozen, this one is frozen on purpose, the conservative signature made sculpture.

entry.name: Fluid Form
entry.description: Morphing iridescent form for φ>0 zone. Embraces becoming.

dna.default: flux=mixed - mixed returns (noise_gain 1.0, sway_gain 0.3), which are the two constants the vertex function carried inline, so the shader computes exactly the code as written. flux needs no rebuild at all - it is two uniforms - and apply_grid_config returns untouched when a config carries none of its keys, which the one existing placement (QFEP_Phi_Term) does not. THE DEFAULT PRESERVES THE CODE PATH BUT NOT WHAT THAT ROOM LOOKED LIKE. See shader_fix; the change was unavoidable and is stated plainly rather than buried.
dna.shader_fix: THE SHADER DID NOT COMPILE, and had not since the file was written. Two fatal errors: fmod is not a function in Godot's shading language (that is GDScript's and HLSL's name for it - the shader language has mod, and fract is what this code wanted), and vec3(127.1, 311.7, 74.7, 1.0) passes four components to a three-component constructor. So the ShaderMaterial never built and the one shipped placement has been rendering an unshaded sphere, not the morphing iridescent form that the registry description, the artifact's name and its @identity block all describe. The hash line is now the one that works in marble_column.gdshader and random_animated.gdshader in this same repo. Fixing it changes that one room, from broken to intended. Leaving it broken was not an option: an axis living in a vertex shader that does not compile produces four identical frames and an INERT verdict that is a fact about the harness rather than about the design - the exact finished-looking experiment that answers nothing.
dna.was: a sphere plus a morphing shader, with no apply_grid_config at all, so nothing here was reachable from a map token - and the shader did not compile in the first place. The four exports were size, morph_speed, flow_intensity and a colour: dimensions, a rate and decoration.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-04, refused by the runner as NO TURNABLE KNOBS. flow_intensity is this file's own declared critical_parameter and it is the WRONG axis: five intensities photograph as five degrees of lumpiness, which is size wearing a name; morph_speed is worse, because a rate is invisible to a still. The vertex function spends its displacement in two registers at a fixed 1.0 : 0.3 ratio - noise ALONG THE NORMAL, where the skin churns and the body keeps its shape, and one smooth wave through the WHOLE BODY, where the silhouette bends. mixed, skin and sway all spend the same flow_intensity and differ only in which register receives it, so the axis is emphatically not an amount. still spends none and is the control: the same form at phi = 0, which is the comparison the phi>0 / phi<0 pair exists to make. NOT named becoming, although queer_morphology_specimen owns that word for phi and sits in this artifact's own cluster_with list - its values (jarred, cracked, escaped, clouded) are about the JAR, the specimen's relation to the vitrine that classifies it, and this form has no jar. Same theme, different question, different word.
dna.fixture_note: freeze_time pins the shader clock and stops the idle rotation so that every flux value is photographed at the same phase - without it the sweep partly measures which frame the camera happened to catch. It defaults to -1.0, which is live time and the shipped behaviour, and is left UNTYPED on purpose, because a typed float rejects the string a fixture passes before _ready. frag_time follows it into the fragment shader and falls through to TIME whenever freeze_time is negative, so the iridescence is untouched unless a capture asks otherwise.
dna.family: NOT one scene under many names, which was the first thing checked. fluid_form, rigid_sculpture and edge_core are three scenes, three scripts and three generators - a shader-morphed sphere; eleven MeshInstance3D built with SurfaceTool and no _process at all; two spheres plus a GPUParticles3D ring - with 4, 3 and 6 exports respectively. The identical-export-count tell is absent. They are a rhetorical pair (phi>0 against phi<0) plus a third object about lambda, and they honestly take three vocabularies. The real one-scene-many-names family sits next door in this registry: reactive_particle_field, reactive_particles, edge_particles and emergence_zone are four tokens on one .tscn.

entry.qfep_connection: A morphing iridescent form for the φ>0 zone — a shape that embraces becoming, never settling, iridescence as the color of change welcomed. The queer signature made beautiful: not resisting time like the rigid sculpture, but flowing with it, difference as the point rather than the threat.

entry.name: Preserved Pattern
entry.description: Static checkerboard that never changes. Conservative φ<0.

dna.default: motif=checker - checker is the `_:` branch of _is_on() and returns `(x + z) % 2 == 0`, the shipped rule character for character, with the same two materials, the same 0.9/0.3/0.9 cell box and the same cell_size * 0.15 lift on the marked cells. All three placements (QFEP_Phi_Term, Corridor_QFEP_Phi_Term, Curation_Bay_qfeplaboratory_5) are bare tokens; apply_grid_config returns before rebuilding unless a key is present AND differs AND _ready has already built once, and a typo also lands on `_:`, so no room can be blanked by a bad word.
dna.was: three exports - grid_size, cell_size, pattern_color - and no apply_grid_config, so nothing was reachable from a map token. The decision that carries the argument was the literal `(x + z) % 2 == 0` inline in the build loop, under a comment reading Classic checkerboard - stable, predictable, preserved.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-04, refused by the runner as NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The @identity names the critical_parameter as THE ABSENCE OF TIME - there is no _process, no delta, no becoming - and that cannot be an axis, because the evidence is one still PNG and a form that does not move photographs identically to one that does. So the axis is the other half of the claim. The artifact says phi<0 preserves a pattern at the cost of life and then never says WHICH pattern, as though there were only one - which is precisely the move a conservative order makes about its own conventions. The checkerboard is not the pattern; it is one inherited draft among several, frozen. Naming the choice is the promotion, and `blank` is the value that finishes the argument: the grid still perfectly regular, still immortal, with nothing left in it to preserve.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: pattern_tile_puzzle (and the five sibling tokens on that scene: _4x4, _mirror, _8x8, _brick, _herringbone). `motif` = blank|checker|cross|twill|houndstooth, the same five words for the same question - which figure a square grid of cells carries - and the arithmetic is reproduced cell for cell, so the two artifacts measure ALIKE: checker is (x+z)%2==0, twill is (x+z)%4<2, cross is the centre row and column, houndstooth is the same 4x4 bitmap tiled. Only the DEFAULT differs, because the loom ships `blank` (it arrives empty, waiting to be edited) and this museum piece ships `checker` (the draft it will keep forever) - which is itself the difference between the two artifacts stated in one word. NOT `dyelot`, pattern_tile's second axis: this grid runs on two materials, not eight yarns, so there is nothing to re-dye.
dna.not_shared_with: random_cubes, its opposite number in this same batch, which took `macrostate` (uniform|corner|layered|spilled) from microstate_counter. The two ARE the two ends of one conceptual line - frozen order against high entropy - and putting them on one shared scale was the tempting move. Refused: the values of such a scale would be DEGREES OF NOISE, an amount wearing a name, and neither artifact's own hidden constant is an amount. One is a draft, the other is a region. A pattern has no macrostate and a loose pile has no motif; they are different terms of the formula (phi against E(S)) on different substrates. edge_core refused a shared word across terms yesterday on exactly this reasoning.
dna.measurement_risk: A THIN FLAT PLATE. The grid is 0.36 m across and about 0.03 m tall, so a fit-by-diagonal camera frames 0.51 m and the plate is foreshortened further by the sweep's slight downward angle - the classic wide-flat dilution case. framing 0.85 brings the fit to about 0.43 m, still wider than the 0.36 m plate so no corner is cropped. The axis lives in WHICH cells are lit and raised, which is the whole face of the subject rather than a detail inside it, so the bite should be strong; if it reads faint, crop-recheck before believing the verdict.

entry.qfep_connection: A checkerboard that never changes — φ<0 made flat and eternal. Conservation as a value: the pattern that has decided the past was correct and the future is a threat. The equation's other resistance, not to disorder but to time.

entry.name: Transforming Pattern
entry.description: Constantly evolving wave pattern. Queer φ>0 signature.

dna.default: concert=superposition - the `_:` branch of _combined() is the three inline waves term for term, sin(t + x*0.8 + z*0.3) + cos(t*1.3 + x*0.4 - z*0.7) + sin(t*0.7 - x*0.5 + z*0.9) over 3, so the 1 existing placement moves cell for cell as it always has. phase_lock defaults to -1.0, which is the free-running clock; the fixture pins it only on the bench.
dna.was: One unnamed wave field, three incommensurate sines averaged inline in _process, driving height, scale, hue and spin. No exports reachable from a map token: there was no apply_grid_config at all.

entry.qfep_connection: A constantly evolving wave pattern — the φ>0 queer signature in motion. Where the preserved checkerboard freezes, this one refuses to hold still, its identity located in transformation rather than persistence. The equation's third term made visible: what matters here is the rate of change, and this pattern has chosen to change.

entry.name: Lambda Promenade
entry.description: The eight promoted QFEP bodies as one walkable line: icon-scale emblems in λ order on a 4.34 m rail, each rebuilding its source at that source's own default, with the λ value etched on every plinth and the F and E(S) poles at the ends. A SERIES synthesis.

relationships.finding: Eight QFEP artifacts were promoted separately in one week and four came back with the SAME finding, independently: an object whose whole claim is about a POSITION had only ever been able to draw one position. [[edge_core]] said it plainest — you cannot see that the edge is NARROW if the two things it is narrow between are never in the room — and that sentence is what this artifact is built out of. The promenade is the missing second term made architectural: the neighbours a body is a position RELATIVE TO, standing in the same room, at icon scale, in λ order, on one rail.

sources.preserved_pattern: [[preserved_pattern]] learned that φ<0 does not merely resist change, it defends a PARTICULAR order — the artifact argued that a pattern is preserved and never said which pattern, 'which is exactly the move a conservative order makes about its own conventions'. Exhibited at λ 0.00 as a 6x6 checkerboard built by its own motif=checker rule, (x + z) % 2 == 0, marked cells raised by cell_size * 0.15, in its own two materials.
sources.rigid_sculpture: [[rigid_sculpture]] learned the same thing about a made monument: five formations are five orders worth defending, and 'the absence of animation cannot be an axis, because a form that does not move and a form that does are the same photograph'. Exhibited at λ 0.05 (qfep_reactor's ORDER_LAMBDA, CRYSTALLINE by its own get_state_name) as its shipped formation=ring: octahedron core, eight prisms on a circle at radius size*0.6 each turned outward, two caps.
sources.edge_core: [[edge_core]] learned that its set_lambda() is called by NOTHING in the repository, so in all three rooms the core stands green and alive for every value of λ there is — an object that can only ever draw the answer is the contradiction of the claim it is there to make. Exhibited at λ 0.40 as station=edge: translucent shell, bright counter-core, and the orbiting ring as what a still of a GPUParticles3D ring actually is, twenty dots, seeded at its own SCATTER_SEED.
sources.qfep_reactor: [[qfep_reactor]] learned the same disease independently in a second file the same day — _connect_to_sliders() waits on a group nothing ever joins, so current_lambda has stood at 0.4 everywhere, forever. Exhibited at λ 0.40 beside edge_core as station=edge, the smooth orb with its emission-sphere cloud at the source's own 0.35-to-0.30 ratio. It also supplies this artifact's second axis: `readout`, taken whole.
sources.transforming_pattern: [[transforming_pattern]] learned that the honest axis between it and preserved_pattern — the presence or absence of time — is exactly the axis a still cannot see, and declined it on the evidence, taking `concert` instead: not whether the grid changes but WHO CHANGES WITH WHOM. Exhibited at λ 0.55 as concert=superposition photographed at phase_lock = 2.0, the phase its own bench fixture pins.
sources.fluid_form: [[fluid_form]] learned that its own declared critical_parameter was the wrong axis — 'five intensities photograph as five degrees of lumpiness, which is size wearing a name' — and that its shader had never compiled, so the one shipped room had been rendering a bare sphere. Exhibited at λ 0.65 as flux=mixed: the fixed noise_gain 1.0 / sway_gain 0.3 pair evaluated on the CPU at freeze_time = 3.0, at the source's own body radius so the noise samples the same field.
sources.random_cubes: [[random_cubes]] learned that entropy is not a property of a pile but a count of the ways it could have been, so the count does not exist until you say WHICH macrostate you are counting — and that the invisible spawn box had to be drawn, because a confined pile without its frame reads as 'a smaller pile over there, which is size wearing a name'. That lesson is why this artifact's rail is always full length. Exhibited at λ 0.85 as macrostate=uniform, chance=all, REPLAYED from its own bench seed rather than modelled.
sources.particle_chaos: [[particle_chaos]] was found HOLLOW: an @export_enum and thirty lines specifying five silhouettes, with _build_particles() constructing the unconstrained cloud regardless — a sweep would have rendered five identical frames and called the axis inert, which would have been a fact about a missing function. Implemented, its lesson is that freedom is invisible with nothing to be free FROM. Exhibited at λ 1.00 (its own header: 'λ = 1 dissolution zone') as constraint=none: the isotropic ball, modelled as a still because the source's cloud lives on the GPU.

relationships.does_not_replace: The eight originals stay placed and keep their own axes. The promenade never re-runs a member's axis from the outside — each emblem is fixed at its source's OWN default — because letting a map drive them from here would fork eight vocabularies into a ninth. This is an addition for rooms that want the comparison, not an upgrade; the walk-scale encounter with one artifact alone is still the curriculum's spine, and it is what the synthesis hides.
relationships.refused_by_a_source: [[edge_core]]'s promotion explicitly declined to share `station` with [[fluid_form]] and [[rigid_sculpture]]: 'their line is phi (resist vs embrace change) and this one's is lambda (order vs chaos)... a shared word with two vocabularies would claim a kinship the geometry does not have.' That is a refusal of exactly the composition this artifact makes. It is therefore made EXPLICITLY and marked in geometry: at readout=lattice each standing body gets a marker at its TRUE (λ, φ) and a tie-line from its slot, and four of the eight tie-lines run off the λ axis because four of these bodies are φ arguments the promenade has projected. The equal spacing is likewise a lie about λ — 0.00 and 0.05 are one slot apart, and so are 0.40 and 0.40 — and the same tie-lines say so.

dna.default: extent=full, readout=numeral. A synthesis has no shipped placements, so the default is a design choice rather than a preservation duty, and this is the strongest single reading: all eight bodies up, in λ order, on the full rail, with both poles standing and the λ number etched on every plinth. It is the only value of `extent` at which the promenade is a spectrum rather than a sample. readout=numeral is the family's legacy rung and matches qfep_reactor, line, xyz_slider_plate and qfep_calibrator; it is also the rung the exhibit needs to be honest at all, since without the numbers the equal spacing passes unchallenged.
dna.was: synthesized from preserved_pattern, rigid_sculpture, edge_core, qfep_reactor, transforming_pattern, fluid_form, random_cubes and particle_chaos — eight artifacts promoted separately between 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-04, whose cross-member argument (that they are positions relative to one another) existed only in registry notes and in one sentence of edge_core's promotion.
dna.axis_extent: WHICH STRETCH OF THE λ LINE IS STOOD UP. The rail is ALWAYS full length and the occupied band is inlaid brighter on it — random_cubes' lesson taken directly, since without the full rail a crop would read as a smaller exhibit instead of a cropped one. full = all eight, the spectrum. ordered_half = λ 0.0..0.5, the four low bodies re-spread over the same rail at twice the size, F pole standing and no E pole. edge = λ 0.3..0.5, which is is_at_edge()'s own interval — the one qfep_reactor has always tested for and never drawn — leaving two bodies on a full-length rail with NEITHER POLE in the room. dissolved_half = λ 0.5..1.0, E(S) pole only. `edge` is the value that argues: with nothing to be an edge between, the edge is not narrow, it is everything.

entry.name: Grasp Cabinet
entry.description: Six compartments, three over three. Five hold the SAME 56 mm object under the `grasp` family's five theories of its handle — atom, socket, chorus, hollow, swarm — read live out of qfep_term_grasp.gd's own const and never retyped. The sixth holds the ledger. A hand at true human scale (18 mm fingertip pads, a 15 mm finger, a 158 mm opening span) closes on all five at once, and `contact` changes what that hand is: a palm cupping from below on eight golden-angle pads, a two-point pinch across the equator, three fingers hooking up from underneath, or a twelve-point icosahedral net closing from every side. `closure` changes how much of the closing is drawn: the hand open and nothing claimed; plus a mark where each contact actually stopped; plus the track it swept getting there; plus the ledger, five rows of bars above and below a rule at the thing's own nominal surface. Nothing animates, nothing is grabbable, nothing is random: one closure computed per theory at build time from one part list, and that same part list is what gets drawn.
interactions: find the two compartments a hand cannot tell apart, and work out why
set contact=pinch and notice that the socket and the wireframe hold your fingers out at almost exactly the same place, 0.28 mm apart, for completely different reasons
set contact=net and read the socket's twelve bars: four at the rim, four on the dome, four down among the ribs — one object, three answers
set closure=depth and see that the only theory whose bars go ABOVE the rule is the one with nothing to pick up
walk the top row against the bottom row and ask which of the five is a claim about the object and which is a claim about its neighbours
entry.qfep_connection: Five theories of where a handle lives — in the object, in its bounded absence, in the set it belongs to, in its outline, in a distribution — standing at once so that none of them can pass as the natural one. The cabinet cannot exempt itself: six compartments holding five claims IS a housing, and a housing is what `socket` says the grip belongs to, so the most innocent-looking piece of furniture in the room is already taking one of the five sides. What the hand then shows is that the affordance was never a property of the object at all. Change nothing about the thing and change only what closes on it, and four of the five readings rearrange; change to a grip that never leaves the body's own surface and two of the five theories become indistinguishable, not because they agree but because one of them was never talking about the body.

Both are named because they call for opposite handling under trimming: dropping the tail of a parallel axis loses a case, dropping the tail of a nested one only lowers the ceiling. `contact` is declared FIRST for exactly that reason — build_dna_gallery sweeps the first two axes and trims the LATER one from the tail.
dna.default:
contact=palm, closure=closed. A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so there is nothing to preserve and the default is a free design choice; the rule that outranks everything in doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md governs promotions of placed artifacts and has no work to do here. That freedom was spent on the strongest single reading rather than the emptiest.

WHY `palm` AND NOT `net`. `net` is the fullest grip and the wrong default: twelve pads plus twelve marks per compartment surround the body so completely that the five theories are largely hidden behind the hand, and a cabinet whose exhibit is obscured by its own instrument is showing the instrument. `palm` comes from BELOW, so the top of every body is clear in every compartment and the five theories are all legible at a glance, while the eight contacts are still enough to show a profile rather than a point. It is also the grip a 56 mm sphere actually invites. `pinch` is the thinnest — two contacts, and they land at the equator where all five theories put their outermost material, so it is the grip that separates them LEAST (four of its ten theory pairs are under 3 mm). `hook` is an insertion rather than a closure and is a special case, not a baseline.

WHY `closed` AND NOT `depth`. `depth` is the most striking single frame and the most misleading one: it ranks the five theories by how far in the hand got, and on that ranking `swarm` wins outright — the one theory of the five where there is nothing whatever to carry off. A scoreboard that calls the emptiest claim the best grip is a fact about scoreboards, which is why it is one token away rather than the frame a visitor meets first. `closed` shows the open pad and the shut pad together, so the whole closure is legible without a single added mark and nothing is asserted that is not shown. `none` is the emptiest rung by definition: a hand held open around five objects and no answer.
dna.was: did not exist. Nothing was promoted here and no shipped behaviour was touched. This is the cross-member argument the five `grasp` declarations leave unbuilt — and in this family it is not merely unbuilt but unbuildable, because all five names are one scene: a single sphere can only be one of atom, socket, chorus, hollow or swarm at a time, so no member can ever put two of the five side by side.
dna.kin:
THE ONE-SCENE-MANY-NAMES CASE, VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. All five tokens that declare `grasp` resolve to res://commons/primitives/point/grab_sphere_point_with_color.tscn — one distinct scene across five names. The tell the corpus keeps rediscovering is identical export counts across siblings, and here it is exact by construction: the scene's four scripts (grab_sphere.gd 10, point_mesh.gd 1, point_color.gd 2, qfep_term_grasp.gd 1) give every one of the five tokens the same 14 exports, and all five carry the same `parameters` block (footprint, size_group). Four of them additionally carry a `default_params.color` that distinguishes them — FF6060, 4080FF, 40FF80, FF80FF — and the fifth, the plain primitive grab_sphere_point_with_color, carries none. That is the entire difference between the five names.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THIS CABINET. When a shared vocabulary is honest the siblings measure ALIKE; here they cannot measure otherwise, because they ARE the same object. So the family's `grasp` axis has, strictly, one subject and five labels for it, and the interesting question is not whether the siblings agree but whether the five VALUES do anything distinguishable — which is what this cabinet answers, and the answer is that two of them do not, under any grip.

THE WORD IS TAKEN WHOLE AND NOT RETYPED. grasp_cabinet.gd opens with
const GRASP_SRC := preload("res://commons/primitives/point/qfep_term_grasp.gd")
and the bays, their number and their order come from GRASP_SRC's own GRASPS at build time, read as a direct const access rather than through Object.get() — a const is not a property, so get() would return null and the cabinet would fall back silently to its own copy, which is the exact drift the preload prevents. get_script_constant_map() was considered and rejected: it is non-static and cannot be called on the class. _check_family_list() runs at _ready and push_errors in BOTH directions: a value the family declares that this cabinet has no bay for, and a bay this cabinet builds that the family has dropped.

ONE DECLARATION ORDER, NO DIVERGENCE. Unlike `taxonomy`, which had two orders across seven members, all five `grasp` declarations list atom | socket | chorus | hollow | swarm character for character — which follows trivially from their being one scene. There is no trimming hazard on the family word.

SOLIDITY IS BORROWED FROM THE FAMILY TOO, and this is the borrowing that does the most work. qfep_term_grasp.gd's _mat(c, energy, alpha) enters its transparency branch iff alpha < 1.0. That one line is taken as the family's own definition of a surface that is there, and this cabinet's probe reads it: the socket's lower shell is alpha 0.55 and a hand passes through it; the swarm's outer two shells are 0.92 and 0.72 and a hand passes through those too, so only the innermost twelve grains stop anything; everything else is 1.0 and stops a hand. Nothing about what is SOLID here was chosen by this artifact.
dna.note:
THE ARGUMENT, AND WHY IT NEEDS A CABINET RATHER THAN A MEMBER.

The family's five words are five claims about where the handle of a thing lives. `atom` says in the object: one closed pellet, uncuttable, self-identical. `socket` says in a bounded absence: half a body and half a measured void behind a bright rim. `chorus` says in the set: the thing is one of four on a rail and you lift the row when you lift it. `hollow` says in the outline: the substance is gone and the contour survives, and your hand closes on a contour. `swarm` says in a distribution: no body at all, a graded population you could be inside rather than an object you could carry off. Five registry names declare this word and every one of them STANDS IN one claim and forgoes the other four — and because all five names are ONE SCENE, that is not a habit but a hard limit. No member can ever hold two of these at once.

So the cabinet builds the thing ONCE — a 56 mm sphere, one colour, one radius — and stands it five times in the family's own order, read live from qfep_term_grasp.gd. What varies instead is the SECOND decision every one of these claims makes and none of them states: what closes on it. A handle is only a handle relative to a grasper, and the family draws no grasper at all.

WHAT IT FOUND, all of it computed in Python before anything was built.

(1) A HAND CANNOT TELL `atom` FROM `chorus`. Under all four grips the two bays return penetration profiles identical to the bit — 0.00 mm, not 0.00-to-two-decimals — because chorus does not touch the body. Read the family's own code: `atom` returns before the match and leaves the shipped SphereMesh alone; `chorus` also leaves `mesh` alone, sets material_override and adds a rail BESIDE it. Every other value replaces the mesh or effaces it. So of the five theories, exactly one makes no claim about the object at all, and it is unfalsifiable by touch — which is not the same as being wrong. THIS IS THE FINDING, NOT A DEAD BAY. The two compartments still look nothing alike.

(2) THE WIREFRAME HOLDS YOUR HAND OUT FURTHER THAN THE SOLID BALL DOES, which is the opposite of the obvious reading. `hollow` measures -11.52 mm against `atom`'s -9.00 under pinch and net. The family builds its rings as tori of ring radius R and tube 0.090 R, so the cage stands 1.09 R proud of the surface it describes, and a fingertip meets wire 2.52 mm before it would have met ball. An outline is not an opening.

(3) `socket` IS THE ONLY ONE WHOSE ANSWER DEPENDS ON WHICH SIDE YOU COME FROM. Palm from below: -2.69 to -1.04, mean -2.100. Pinch at the equator: -11.80, the furthest OUT of any theory under any grip, because the rim's outer surface is at 1.10 R. Net from all sides: a three-tier reading of -11.80 (four pads on the rim), -9.00 (four on the dome) and -3.42 to -3.26 (four down among the ribs). A swing of 14.4 mm on one object. The other four theories are isotropic; this one is a fragment and reports as one.

(4) `socket` AND `hollow` MEASURE ALIKE UNDER `pinch`, 0.28 mm APART, AND IT IS A COINCIDENCE WORTH KEEPING. The socket's rim reaches 1.10 R and the hollow's great circles reach 1.09 R, so a two-point grip at the equator is held out at nearly the same place by a bright flange and by a wire. Two completely different theories, one number. Nothing was tuned to produce this and nothing will be tuned to remove it.

(5) THE ONLY THEORY A HAND GETS INSIDE IS THE ONE WITH NOTHING TO HOLD. `swarm` returns positive penetration under every grip, +2.70 to +6.91 mm, because its outer two shells are drawn transparent and a hand passes through them to the twelve opaque grains at 0.42 R. It is the deepest reading in the cabinet and it is a reading of a cloud. That is precisely why `depth` is not the default.

AND TWO FAULTS IN THE INSTRUMENT, BOTH CAUGHT BY THE REPLICA AND BOTH THE SAME FAULT.

(a) The `net`'s twelve directions were first taken from the family's own _fib_points(12) — which is exactly how the swarm's inner shell of twelve grains is built. All twelve probes ran straight down the twelve grain axes and returned one number to the millimetre. Replaced with the twelve icosahedron vertices.

(b) The `palm`'s eight pads were first spaced evenly at 45 degrees — which is exactly the spacing of the socket's eight ribs. Every pad landed on a rib and the bay reported -2.69 mm with a standard deviation of 0.000. Offsetting by half a step is not a fix: all eight then slip between the ribs and report +0.02 mm, sd 0.000 — a swing of 2.71 mm and a change of SIGN, still an artefact. At golden-angle azimuths the same eight pads read -2.69 to -1.04, mean -2.100, sd 0.564. The hollow bay tells the same story more quietly: sd 0.000 at even azimuths, 0.345 at golden. A measuring instrument built out of the thing it measures will report perfect uniformity and be believed, twice in one file.
dna.declines:
`grasp` IS REFUSED AS THIS ARTIFACT'S AXIS, on the record, and the refusal is the design.

The five values sit SIDE BY SIDE, read out of the member's CODE and not its prose. qfep_term_grasp.gd spends the word in a single `match grasp:` whose branches are mutually exclusive treatments of ONE mesh: atom returns before the match and keeps it; socket REPLACES `mesh` with a hemisphere; chorus keeps it and adds a rail beside it; hollow and swarm both call _efface_body() and add rings or grains. Three different fates for one mesh — kept, replaced, effaced — so no value contains another and there is no all-at-once reading that is secretly the top rung. Parallel values means the simultaneity is the object: hold all five standing and vary something else. An axis on the word would demolish four fifths of the exhibit at every turn, and the big number it produced would be a measurement of the cabinet being dismantled.

THREE CORRECTIONS TO THE HANDED-DOWN READING OF THE WORD. The brief this artifact was built from glossed the five values, and on three of them the code says something else. The code wins and the correction is recorded here.
  `socket` was glossed as "a receptacle — the grip belongs to the housing, not to the object". There is no housing anywhere in the family's socket. What the code builds is a solid upper hemisphere, a bright rim torus at the equator, a lower hemisphere of radius 0.985 R drawn at alpha 0.55, and eight ribs from rim to south pole. It is HALF A BODY AND A BOUNDED VOID: the receptacle is part of the object, and the object is admitting it is a fragment and showing exactly how much of it is not there.
  `chorus` was glossed as "many identical handles where any will do". The family's siblings are the OTHER THREE TERMS of QFE = F - lambda*E(S) + phi*deltaE(S,t), in their own registry colours, in the formula's written order — the whole point being that they are NOT interchangeable and that lifting one lifts a structured set. See below for what this cabinet had to give up to transpose that.
  `hollow` was glossed as "a grip defined by what is absent, the space your hand goes into". Half right. The code keeps the OUTLINE and destroys the substance, so a hand closes on a contour rather than into a recess — and this cabinet measures that the contour is 2.52 mm PROUD of the surface it describes, so the hollow thing is harder to reach into than the full one. The prose predicts a recess; the geometry delivers a cage.

WHAT THE CHORUS BAY GAVE UP, stated rather than buried. Three deviations from the family's numbers, all forced by there being one thing here and no formula.
  The siblings are the same colour as the body, dimmed, where the family gives them three different hexes. There is no formula, so there are no other terms; four copies of one thing is the honest transposition and what it loses is exactly the claim the family's chorus makes best.
  CHOR_SPAN is 1.25 R against the family's 2.7 R and CHOR_OVER 0.35 R against 0.9 R. At the family's pitch the rail is 9.9 R wide, which would set the width of all six compartments and leave five of them four fifths air.
  CHOR_RAIL_Y is -3.6 R against the family's -2.4 R, and this one is not cosmetic. The hand's opening envelope is a sphere of radius 3.143 R about the body; the nearest sibling sits 1.25 R aside with radius 0.60 R, so the rail must drop until sqrt(1.25^2 + y^2) - 0.60 > 3.143 + 0.321, i.e. |y| > 3.527 R. At the family's -2.4 R the hand's own opening position is INSIDE the rail and the cabinet would be drawing a hand embedded in furniture. THE COST IS FINDING (1): with the rail out of reach, nothing the hand does can distinguish chorus from atom. That cost is reported, not hidden, and it was measured rather than assumed.

THE RECURSION WAS CONSIDERED AND DECLINED, and it is the interesting decline. Six compartments holding five theories IS a housing, and a housing is what one of the five theories says the grip belongs to — so the cabinet is standing inside the question it asks, exactly as taxonomy_hall's row of bays is itself the table claim. It could have gone further and applied the family word to its own compartments. It does not, for the mechanical reason taxonomy_hall gives: the registry would then carry a sixth `grasp` declaration with the same five values as the other five, and every tool that groups a family by axis name would compare its bite against theirs as though it measured the same thing. It does not: theirs restage a BODY, this one would restage a CABINET. So the recursion is stated in prose and not swept.

PER-BAY CAPTIONS ARE DECLINED. There is no text anywhere in this artifact. At 1021.84 px per metre a legible glyph would be about 1.2 cm tall, a fifth of the object's diameter, and there is no surface in a compartment to hang it on that is not in front of a mark. Identity is carried by the geometry: no two bays share a silhouette.

A `scale` AXIS WAS CONSIDERED AND DECLINED — the same hand at four sizes, which is a real question about affordance and would have been a second axis about the hand. Refused because two axes both about the grasper would leave the exhibit itself never varying in any respect, and because the honest version of it is a single fact better stated once: at the family's own 24 mm a human fingertip pad is 75% of the object's diameter and there are not four distinguishable grips to be had. That is why this cabinet's thing is 56 mm.
dna.measured: PREDICTION HIT, EXACTLY. Swept 2026-08-13 at --max=16, all sixteen frames. Closest pair 0.16% of frame at subject 46.8% — and the registry had named that pair before any capture: `closure` closed against travel AT `contact` = pinch, predicted 0.11% frame. Right pair, 1.5x on the number. The arithmetic holds up: at pinch there are two contacts per compartment, so `travel` adds ten stems of roughly 364 px each against a 625x582 crop — about one percent of it. At `hook` the same pair has fifteen stems and is wider. NOT THE FURNITURE-IN-FRONT CASE despite looking exactly like it: 46.8% subject with a 0.16% pair is the signature that table row warns about, and here the carcass is honest load-bearing furniture — six bays are what lets five theories of the grip stand at once — and nothing occludes a mark. Checked against the PNG, not inferred. Left alone.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in the critic's own currency rather than in changed pixels, because a prediction in the wrong units is a prediction about a different instrument. The critic crops to the union of the two frames' subject boxes, neutralises each frame's own background, converts to greyscale, RESIZES TO 160 x 160 and takes the mean of the hottest 5% (1,280 samples). Every number below comes from rasterising this exact geometry at this exact camera (FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, 760 x 760, dna.framing 0.52) in Python with a painter's depth sort and pushing the result through that same pipeline.

THE CLOSEST PAIR IS `closure` closed <-> travel, AT `pinch`, PREDICTED 2.13% FOCUS / 0.11% FRAME. The arithmetic: the `travel` rung adds one stem per contact, and at pinch there are two contacts per compartment, so the whole cabinet gains TEN stems. Each is 8.28 px wide and about 44 px long in screen, i.e. roughly 364 px, so 3,640 px on a subject crop of 625 x 582 = 363,750 px — one percent of the crop, at a contrast of about 120 grey levels against the compartment interior. The second closest is the same pair at `hook` (three contacts, fifteen stems), predicted 2.74%.

THAT PAIR IS ALSO THIS PASS'S OWN CRITICISM OF ITSELF. Grouped by VALUE PAIR across all four contacts rather than by context — which is how a conditional axis must be read — `closed|travel` is the weakest rung transition at 5.12% mean, against `none|depth` at 18.85%. The reason is not a drawing failure: the open pad and the shut pad are BOTH visible from the `closed` rung on, so the travel is already legible as the gap between them, and the stem only names it. If the sweep confirms it, the finding is that `travel` is a nearly redundant rung and it should be recorded as such rather than trimmed out of the declaration in advance to flatter the axis mean.

AXIS MEANS PREDICTED, over the 24 same-axis pairs each: `contact` 2.17% frame / 28.69% focus -> BITES comfortably. `closure` 0.63% frame / 11.40% focus -> lands on the WEAK/BITES line at 12%, and I expect the real capture to come in ABOVE the prediction rather than below it, because the replica renders flat Lambert shading with NO emission at all while every closed pad and every ledger bar in the artifact is emissive cyan at 1.4x. If `closure` comes back under 12%, that is not a harness fault and should be reported as measured.

`closure` IS CONDITIONAL ON THE PROBE COUNT, by a factor of four, and must be grouped by value pair rather than by context mean. Its pairs run 10.66-32.54% at `net` (twelve contacts per compartment) and 2.13-9.38% at `pinch` (two). That is structural, not accidental: every mark this axis adds is one per contact, so the axis is exactly as loud as the grip is many-fingered.

WIDEST PAIR ON THE SHEET, predicted: `contact` hook <-> net at closure=depth, 36.21%. THINNEST `contact` pair: pinch <-> hook at closure=none, 9.89% — two pads at the equator against three at the underside, with no marks drawn yet.

AND ONE PAIR PREDICTED **NOT** TO BE DEGENERATE, because it looks like it should be. `atom` and `chorus` return penetration profiles identical to the bit under every grip, so the obvious expectation is that those two compartments photograph alike. They do not, and the difference is not subtle: the chorus bay carries three 34.33 px siblings, a 5.72 px rail 143 px long and a 5.72 px riser 62 px tall, none of which exists in the atom bay. The theories are indistinguishable to a hand and not remotely indistinguishable to a camera, which is the whole of finding (1). If a future reader crops to those two bays and reports them as twins, they will have measured the argument and called it a bug.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB, which here is also every individual variant's AABB: the carcass encloses everything either axis can draw, so the box is 0.57616 x 0.44592 x 0.18944 in all sixteen frames. Diagonal sqrt(0.331960 + 0.198845 + 0.035888) = 0.752790, radius 0.376395. The rig is dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) x PAD x framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so framing 1.0 puts the camera at 0.376395 / 0.3057307 x 1.9 = 2.33915 m and shows a 1.43030 m frame around a 0.576 m object — PAD 1.9 already shows 1.9x the bounding-sphere radius, which is why a bench object wants framing well below 1.0.

AT 0.52 the camera comes to 1.21636 m and the frame to 0.743756 m, which is 1021.84 px per metre. From this standpoint a horizontal along X projects at cos(0.62) = 0.81388, a vertical at cos(0.26) = 0.96639, and depth contributes -0.58104 to screen x and -0.20923 to screen up. The subject's screen box is therefore 0.81388 x 0.57616 + 0.58104 x 0.18944 = 0.57907 m wide by 0.96639 x 0.44592 + 0.20923 x 0.18944 = 0.55065 m tall, i.e. 77.9% of frame width and 74.0% of height, leaving 84 px of clear margin on each side. Rasterised, the union subject box measures 82.2% of frame width by 76.6% of height (the drawn content overhangs the analytic box slightly because the hand's pads are spheres tangent to the compartment walls) and the subject covers 16.85% of the frame at the default tile — well above the ~6% dilution floor and above the blank-render check. 0.50 was measured too (81.0% of width) and rejected: 72 px of margin is thinner than the showcase key light's specular fringe, which the replica does not model.

GAUGE CHECK AT 1021.84 px/m, because foresight_range shipped a bench's 0.028 m arrows onto an 18 m lane and sorting_hall drew a whole axis three pixels wide. THE AXES' OWN MARKS FIRST, since those are the ones a verdict is about: fingertip pad 0.018 m -> 18.39 px; finger 0.015 -> 15.33 px; the pad's swept track 0.0081 -> 8.28 px; ledger bar 0.00804 wide -> 8.22 px and 0.01463 tall at the largest reading -> 14.95 px, on a 43.16 px row pitch, against a ceiling gauge 35.48 px tall. Nothing either axis draws is under 8 px.

THE EXHIBIT'S OWN MARKS, which are constant across both axes and are the family's ratios rather than this artifact's choices: the thing 0.056 m -> 57.22 px; socket rim outer 0.0616 -> 62.95 px with a 4.58 px tube; socket rib 0.0042 -> 4.29 px; hollow ring tube 0.00504 -> 5.15 px and latitude tube 0.00403 -> 4.12 px; swarm grain 0.00924 -> 9.44 px; chorus sibling 0.0336 -> 34.33 px on a 5.72 px rail; carcass panel 0.00784 -> 8.01 px. The four-pixel marks are the socket's ribs and the hollow's latitudes, and they are kept at the family's own 0.075 R and 0.072 R rather than thickened: the family sized those explicitly to survive a capture, they are part of the exhibited body and not a gauge of this artifact's, and they are constant in all sixteen tiles. Recorded rather than fixed.

THE CABINET IS 3 x 2 AND NOT A ROW OF SIX, and that was a framing decision with a number. Six compartments in a line gives a union 6.3x wider than tall, a screen box of 30.5 R by 6.2 R, and at 78% frame fill only 259 px/m — every mark 2.5x smaller, with the socket's ribs at 1.7 px. Occlusion, which is what pushed taxonomy_hall into a row, does not bite here: the compartments are 0.211 m tall and the shelves 0.0078 m thick, so at a 15-degree downward pitch a shelf hides 5.7 mm of the compartment below it, which is the empty air under a body that sits 0.0148 m above the compartment centre.
dna.fixture_note:
NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED IS NEEDED, and it is checkable rather than claimed. The file contains no randf, no randi, no randomize, no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween, no physics body and no reference to the scene tree outside its own children. _ready is ungated: it reads config metadata, checks the family list against the preload, measures, and builds the whole cabinet standalone, so the sweep's rescue path (call apply_grid_config when the AABB measures zero) will never fire.

EVERY POSITION IS ARITHMETIC. The swarm's sixty-eight grains come from the family's own _fib_points, character for character, keyed on the index; the net's twelve directions are the icosahedron's vertices; the palm's eight azimuths are k times the golden angle; the socket's eight ribs are k times a quarter turn. Nothing is rolled and nothing is hashed. Two captures of one value are two photographs of one object.

THE CLOSURE IS DETERMINISTIC TO THE BIT, which is the one place this artifact could have leaked a difference between runs. The probe is sphere-traced against exact distance fields and then BISECTED twenty-four times, so the stop does not depend on the march path. Without the bisection it did: `atom` and `chorus` are the same body to a hand, and they came out 0.02 mm apart purely because chorus's riser is nearer at the start and shortened one early step. A residue of the instrument, reported as a difference between two theories.

THE SORT IS DETERMINISTIC BY CONSTRUCTION. Godot's Array.sort_custom is not stable, so _sorted_pen does not use it: it runs a hand-rolled selection sort over at most twelve elements whose comparison is (value, index) and therefore TOTAL, so there is nothing for stability to decide.

THREE WAYS IN, ONE DOOR. The sweep sets the @export directly before add_child; the grid stamps config_contact / config_closure metadata, which _read_grid_config_meta walks up to four ancestors for before _ready builds; and apply_grid_config takes a dictionary. All three are validated against _is_contact / _is_closure, and apply_grid_config rebuilds ONLY when a value actually changed AND _ready has already built once — the force_pad fault. An unrecognised word keeps the standing value.

BOTH AXES ARE String ENUMS, not bools, so the fixture-string trap (a typed bool rejecting the string "true" before _ready) cannot occur here.
dna.still_note:
WHAT SHOULD BITE AND WHAT SHOULD NOT, said in advance so a thin number is read correctly.

`atom` AND `chorus` ARE THE SAME BODY TO A HAND, BY CONSTRUCTION AND ON PURPOSE. Their penetration profiles are identical to the bit under all four grips. They are NOT the same picture: the chorus bay carries a rail, three siblings and a riser that the atom bay has no equivalent of. If a future reader crops to the readings and reports the pair as degenerate, they will have measured finding (1) and called it a bug. See dna.note.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE OF `closure`: the carcass, all five bodies, and the open pads. Everything that changes between the four closure tiles is the record of the encounter, which is that axis's whole subject. Constant at every value of `contact`: the carcass and all five bodies. Nothing about the exhibit ever moves; only the hand does.

THE SIXTH COMPARTMENT IS EMPTY OF BARS AT THREE OF THE FOUR CLOSURE VALUES, and that is deliberate. It still carries its five rules and its ceiling gauge, so it reads as a ruled page rather than as an unfinished cabinet, and it is the honest picture of a count that has not been asked for.

FOUR OF THE FIVE BAYS HAVE AN EMPTY LOWER THIRD, and it is a cost rather than a fault. The compartment must be tall enough for the chorus bay's rail at -3.6 R, so the body sits 0.0148 m above the compartment centre in every bay and only chorus uses the space beneath. This is why the subject covers 16.85% of frame rather than more; the union box fills 82.2% of frame width, so the framing is not at fault. A sparse subject is not a small one.

NO TEXT ANYWHERE. There is not one Label3D, not one glyph, in any tile — see dna.declines for why. LabelFramer therefore has nothing to hang panels behind, and nothing enters or leaves the capture AABB on that account.

THE CAPTURE AABB IS THE REAL BODY. Every drawn node is a MeshInstance3D holding a BoxMesh, SphereMesh, TorusMesh or CylinderMesh; there is no MultiMeshInstance3D, no CSG and no particle system, so no `layers = 0` anchor is needed and none is present.

IF IT COMES BACK FAINT, check four things before the design.
(1) Was --max at least 16? At the gallery's default cap of 9 a 4x4 declaration renders 4x2 and `closure` is measured on [closed, none] alone — a mean of 8.84% published as a verdict about four rungs. THE FULL SHEET NEEDS --max=16.
(2) Was the sweep run --staged? A 0.58 m cabinet is far under the 6 m staging cut-off, so a plinth would be added under it, the pair AABB would grow and every mark would shrink. In a MAP this artifact does want a table under it — spatial_needs.platform says so — but the sweep should photograph the cabinet alone.
(3) Is the verdict about `closure` rather than about the probe count? That axis is CONDITIONAL by a factor of four, 10.66-32.54% at `net` against 2.13-9.38% at `pinch`, because every mark it draws is one per contact. Group by value pair across contexts, not by context mean.
(4) Is the standpoint doing the work? The five bays rank in screen X and Y and the canonical camera sees the front elevation at 35.5 degrees off its normal, which is the angle at which the compartments' side walls and the chorus rail's depth both read. A probe from straight in front would flatten the rail into the body and one from above would put every hand between the camera and its object. Per the standing gate an INERT verdict on this token is not reportable until tools/probe_anamorphic.py has been run on it.

entry.name: Phi Term Sphere
entry.description: Grabbable sphere representing φ (phi) - the rate sensitivity, the queer signature. Magenta glow.
entry.qfep_connection: φ, the rate sensitivity, glowing magenta — the queer signature, the term that cares not about entropy but about its *rate of change*. Grab it and you hold the project's most particular idea: that what matters is not order or disorder but the system's stance toward becoming, φ>0 embracing change, φ<0 resisting it. The term that makes the equation about time, and desire.
